subject.title: openai-responses transport sends null content, rejected by strict providers (400 schema error)

question: Should OpenClaw accept source-level plus strict-mock SDK proof for a narrow OpenAI Responses null-content send-boundary sanitizer, or require live weelinking-style provider proof before another fix attempt?
rationale: The current source still lacks the sanitizer, but the prior direct fix closed unmerged because no contributor had live strict-provider access; automation should not repeat that loop without maintainer proof-scope intent.

options.title: Accept strict-mock proof for a narrow sanitizer
options.body: Sponsor or allow a focused fix that normalizes only invalid `content: null` at the final Responses send boundary and proves managed OpenAI/Azure paths with regression tests.

options.title: Require live strict-provider proof first
options.body: Keep this as a watchlist item until the original reporter or another operator provides redacted live logs from a strict-compatible endpoint on current main.

options.title: Broaden into strict-provider input sanitization design
options.body: Treat this issue and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100657 as a shared compatibility-design problem before choosing specific fields to strip or coerce.

recommendation.title: Accept strict-mock proof for a narrow sanitizer
recommendation.body: Sponsor or allow a focused fix that normalizes only invalid `content: null` at the final Responses send boundary and proves managed OpenAI/Azure paths with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Azure/OpenAI Responses work makes this the best available routing candidate for the proof-scope and send-boundary behavior choice.
